articles.headline: Falcons release veteran kicker Nick Folk and sign Jake Moody off Ravens' practice squad
keyFacts: The Atlanta Falcons released veteran kicker Nick Folk on Wednesday.
The team signed Jake Moody from the Baltimore Ravens' practice squad to replace Folk.
The roster change follows recent trades involving starters Jessie Bates III and Ryan Neuzil.
body: FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. (AP) — The Atlanta Falcons released kicker Nick Folk and signed Jake Moody off Baltimore's practice squad, they announced Wednesday.

Folk had made 107 consecutive field-goal attempts of inside 40 yards before he was wide left on a 38-yarder in the third quarter of Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals. Folk, 42, was 13 of 18 on field-goal attempts this season, his first with Atlanta, after having only one miss in each of his three previous seasons.
Moody, 26, was activated off the Ravens' practice squad and made a 53-yard field goal in the rain during a 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday.

The release of Folk came after the Falcons traded two starters before Tuesday's trade deadline. On Monday, Atlanta traded safety Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars for a 2027 second-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. On Tuesday, the Falcons sent starting center Ryan Neuzil to the Ravens for offensive lineman Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round draft pick.
The Falcons also activated offensive tackle Cameron Williams from the reserve/injured list to the active roster.

articles.headline: Patriots' Corey Kiner Faces Biggest Test Yet With Rhamondre Stevenson Sidelined
keyFacts: Corey Kiner will likely take a central role in the Patriots' backfield due to Rhamondre Stevenson's multiweek absence.
Coach Mike Vrabel noted that Kiner must improve his recognition of defensive pressure to handle increased responsibilities in pass protection.
The Patriots face the Detroit Lions in Munich this Sunday while managing significant injuries to their running back depth.

The New England Patriots are heading to Munich with a backfield that looks dramatically different from the one they expected to rely on this season. With Rhamondre Stevenson reportedly facing a multiweek absence and TreVeyon Henderson also unavailable recently, Corey Kiner could find himself playing a central role against the Detroit Lions.

Kiner has rushed for 244 yards and one touchdown on 50 carries this season. Those numbers reflect a player who has already contributed, but his responsibilities could increase substantially if New England's injury situation does not improve before Sunday. The Patriots may need him to handle both rushing attempts and demanding assignments in pass protection.

Stevenson's value goes beyond the rushing statistics that appear in a box score. He has been a reliable receiving option and an important part of New England's protection packages, particularly when defenses bring extra pressure against Drake Maye. Replacing those responsibilities is more complicated than simply distributing additional carries.

articles.headline: Honkai Star Rail’s First Playable Aeon Isn’t A Damage God, And That’s A Good Thing
keyFacts: HoYoverse will introduce Aha, the Aeon of Elation, as the first playable Aeon in Honkai Star Rail's Version 4.7 update.
Lead game designer Chengan An stated that Aha is designed as a supportive unit to encourage team synergy rather than dealing extreme damage.
Developers chose Aha because their human-like personality fits a supportive role, preventing the character from making existing units obsolete.
body: The Aeons of Honkai Star Rail have always been far beyond ordinary mortals. They are conceptual deities whose actions have the potential to reshape entire galaxies--so putting one into a player's four-person team was always going to be a huge design challenge for the HoYoverse team.

Ahead of the game's Version 4.7 update, we spoke to lead game designer Chengan An about why Aha, The Aeon of Elation, was chosen as the game's first playable Aeon. According to Chengan, the decision to bring Aha into the fold came down to their uniquely human disposition, as well as the development team's unwillingness to break the game's battle rules. Aha is meant to focus on collaborative synergy rather than racking up extreme damage numbers.

Chengan also noted that Aha's personality is what makes them the most logical Aeon to bring to the battlefield at this point in the game's life cycle. "The game's system is based on the concept of Paths. For Aeons, they are quite abstract concepts for most of the people in the world, but Aha is the most human-like one."

Chengan continued: "I think our [game's] battle is way too tiny for Aeons to initiate a war. For Aha, we picked some of the most important factors to bring into the combat design. We certainly don't want them to destroy the battle with the power of an Aeon, and that kind of design does not fit Aha's personality as an Aeon of Elation."
HoYoverse viewed the Path of Elation as a foundation for Aha, one that's been built up over months of prior updates.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rMcFUTECbMQ

"For the Path of Elation, we do not intend to simply bring a character with super-strong skills to overcome all the existing characters when we have already designed so many previous Paths. We aim to bring the Aeon of Elation to interact with our other characters, and that's why we have already presented so many characters that can interact with Aha. We think this kind of design can bring a fresh experience to our players when they see such an Aeon," Chengan explained.

Chengan confirmed that Aha was never envisioned as an offensive carry, and that the decision to make them a supportive unit rather than a damage dealer was an easy one. "We've always designed Aha that way," he said. "Aha is closely connected to other characters, and from Aha's instance you can see lots of performances. The Path of Elation is about bringing happiness and all these emotions. Aha is more suitable to be a supportive character than a damage-carrying one."

Playing alongside Aha is supposed to mirror stepping onto a grand stage together, reframing the battlefield into an immersive performance. "All the characters together with Aha perform on the cosmic stage, and different characters have their own moments on that stage." Chengan said.

By keeping Aha in a supportive role, HoYoverse avoids rendering previous characters obsolete. Instead of ending the fight single-handedly with absurd damage output, the Aeon of Elation works alongside every squad member, giving them a chance to show their strengths.

This is the best choice HoYoverse could have made when introducing a playable Aeon. Investing years of play time into a game only to have your hard work nullified by introducing an overpowered character that's capable of wiping the floor with any opponent would have put many players, myself included, off the game. However, if this is the approach the team is taking with Aha, I don't foresee any possible ways to add more playable Aeons in the future, unless they exclusively take on support roles, and that could be a missed opportunity.

It remains to be seen whether there are any tricks up HoYoverse's sleeve to get around the limitations they've created for themselves, but for now I'm looking forward to bringing Aha into my team and feeling what it's like to play as an actual deity.

articles.headline: Tributes paid as Cheltenham Festival-winning jockey Tom O’Brien dies
keyFacts: Cheltenham Festival-winning jockey Tom O’Brien has died at age 39 following a battle with cancer.
O’Brien recorded over 1,000 career wins and five Grade One victories during his two-decade career in Britain and Ireland.
Members of the racing community, including former colleagues and the British Horseracing Authority, have paid tribute to O’Brien’s career and character.
body: Tributes have flooded in from across the racing world today following the death of jockey Tom O’Brien at the age of 39 after a battle with cancer.
The Irishman retired from the saddle back in April 2023 and enjoyed an incredible career over two decades, where he rode over 1000 winners across Britain and Ireland.
O’Brien relished victory after riding Third Wind to victory at the 2022 Cheltenham Festival GETTY
O’Brien was also a two-time Cheltenham Festival winner, on board Silk Affair in the 2009 Fred Winter and on mount Third Wind in the 2022 Pertemps Final.
He recorded five Grade One victories throughout his career too, most notably on board Thyme Hill in the 2021 Liverpool Hurdle and 2022 Kauto Star Novices’ Chase.
Alongside his fantastic career, he has also been remembered prominently for the kind of man he was by those who knew him.
The heartbreaking news has spread across the racing world and the tributes have truly captured his legacy and impact.
Former champion jockey Richard Johnson, who rode with O’Brien for many years at Philip Hobbs’ Minehead yard, described his former colleague as an ‘all-round great person.
Johnson told the Press Association: “It’s such sad news and I’m not sure there are any words to describe it really.
“Tom had been ill for quite a while now, but again it doesn’t feel real and I feel very sorry for Hayley and his two little boys.
“Tom was an all-round great person and you won’t find anyone with a bad word to say about him.

“He left a positive mark on all of us. I spent a long time riding with him at Philip Hobbs’ yard and we never had a cross word, and I think that would apply to anyone you speak to as he was just an all-round good man.”
O’Brien joined Hobbs as a teenager after moving from Ireland and remained there until his retirement, eventually taking over as stable jockey following Johnson’s retirement in 2021.
Hobbs said: “He came to our yard from Ireland having not ridden in a race, but it soon became obvious he was pretty talented and he was with us from the start of his career until the end.
“He was in the shadow of Richard Johnson for a long time being second jockey and then became first jockey after Richard retired, which went well.
“His biggest win was Thyme Hill in the Grade One at Aintree and he was always very reliable and a very good bloke.
“There’s lots of good memories and there were lots of winners.”
Jockey Tom O’Brien rode Thyme Hill on his last ever ride before retirement at Sandown Park GETTY
The British Horseracing Authority posted a heartfelt tribute to O’Brien, who joined the stewarding team after retiring from race riding.
Chief executive Brant Dunshea said: “Everyone at the BHA and across British and Irish racing is mourning the devastating loss of our friend and colleague Tom O’Brien.
“Tom passed away surrounded by his loved ones following a long and courageous battle with cancer, which he faced with the steely determination and drive that typified the man so many of us knew.”
The talkSPORT family have also paid tribute.
View Tweet: https://x.com/alex_crook/status/2120434432007967109?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw
View Tweet: https://t.co/s8JOg7Tv3K
Fellow jockey Lizzie Kelly also paid her respects on Racing Live on talkSPORT2.
She said: “It’s really hard to get your head around the journey that Tom went on.

“He retired only three years at the age of 36 after a hugely successful career and his two little boys and wife Hayley probably relieved that he finished race riding and could do something less dangerous with his time only to find out that he had cancer, and it was going to be a really tough battle and he sought out many treatments both here and in America.
She added: “He was a lovely man, he was a really tough competitor, he was a friend to many in the weighing room, past and present.
“I remember him as ultimately being kind and generous. He didn’t shout when you got things wrong. But he’d quietly say something.

“He had a smile that would light up a room, like he had a smile that just made you laugh when you saw him and twinkling in his eye and we had a lot of fun shooting the breeze in the weighing room between races and he was someone I always liked riding against as well.
“He was just a wonderful guy and despite the fact that we all knew that Tom’s health had been declining it’s been really difficult to comprehend how this has happened so quickly.”

articles.headline: How to get the Zora Tunic in Ocarina of Time
keyFacts: The Zora Tunic allows players to explore underwater in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.
Players can obtain the tunic for free by thawing King Zora with blue fire from the Ice Cavern.
Equipping the Zora Tunic with Iron Boots is required to walk freely underwater and complete the Water Temple.
body: Once you get the Zora Tunic in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, you'll be ready to explore the waters of Hyrule. Before you obtain this tunic, the only way to explore underwater is by diving, and even if you have the Golden Scale, Link always has to come up for air. However, after you get the tunic — and a pair of special boots — you'll be able to freely walk under the water. Besides, you must have the tunic to progress the story and complete the Water Temple.
Here's where to get the Zora Tunic in Zelda Ocarina of Time.
Where to get the Zora Tunic in Zelda Ocarina of Time

There are two ways to obtain the Zora Tunic. You can either receive it for free from King Zora as adult Link or buy it from the Shop Owner in Zora Domain for 600 rupees. You should not even think about wasting your rupees doing this, since you can get the tunic from progressing in the main story.

King Zora will reward you with the Zora Tunic after you free him from the ice in Zora Domain during the "Disaster in Zora Domain" quest. Travel to Zora Domain to find that the place — and its citizens — frozen. To progress through the quest, you must go to Zora Fountain, where you previously found Jabu-Jabu, and enter the Ice Cavern dungeon on the north side.

Completing this dungeon rewards you with the Iron Boots. Before leaving the place, be sure to capture a blue fire in an empty bottle. Then, head back to Zora Domain and release the fire next to King Zora to thaw him. After asking Link to once again help his daughter, Princess Ruto, King Zora will give him the Zora Tunic.

Keep in mind that, even while wearing this tunic, if you use the diving command, Link will still come up for air. If you want to stay underwater longer, you must equip the Iron Boots alongside the Zora Tunic.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is a little bit different than the original game, so if you need guides to help you through, we don’t blame you. We have walkthroughs for all the dungeons, from the Deku Tree to Ganondorf's Castle. We also have guides for the sillier, in-between parts of the game, like when you have to find Richard (the dog) or Cuccos.
For those going for 100% completion, we also have guides on where to find every Piece of Heart, every Gold Skulltula token, and where to plant every Magic Bean.

articles.headline: Kioxia has chained together 640 SSDs to create a 157 *petabyte* storage solution, because AI data centers get all the cool toys
keyFacts: Kioxia and Dell created a storage solution by chaining 640 enterprise SSDs to reach 157 petabytes of capacity in one rack.
The system is designed for AI data centers to increase storage density without requiring more floor space, power, or cooling.
This hardware configuration consists of 16 PowerEdge servers packed into a single industry-standard 42U server rack.
body: There's a golden rule of storage: no matter how much you have, it's never quite enough. Nevertheless, Kioxia is taking that principle to its limits, as it's announced "a new storage density milestone" in the form of 640 of its 245.76 TB enterprise SSDs chained together to create just over 157 petabytes worth of storage in a single rack cabinet.
157 petabytes is... well, it's 157 million gigabytes. Enough storage space for God of War: Ragnarok, a 190 GB game, to be installed over 820,000 times.

And yes, it's been designed for AI data centers. The "storage solution" (I do hate that term) has been created in collaboration with Dell, and essentially amounts to 16 PowerEdge R7725xd servers, each stuffed with 40 Kioxia LC9 Series drives inside one industry-standard 42U server rack.

"As AI workloads drive continued growth in unstructured data, organizations need storage that can deliver higher capacity without a corresponding increase in data center floor/rack space, power consumption or cooling requirements," says the press gumph. "High-capacity NVMe SSDs can help address these demands by consolidating more data into a smaller, more efficient infrastructure footprint."

Which seems timely. With physical data center size becoming an increasing issue (not least because massive data center buildouts are a tad unpopular right now), cramming as much storage as possible into a single rack is sure to save on some concrete, at the very least.

But I'm not going to suggest this sort of excessive consumption is anything but jarring, given us little ol' consumers are counting our pennies in the middle of a NAND flash crisis. Have you seen the price of game-ready SSDs recently? I have. It ain't pretty.

But hey, at least we know where 157 petabytes-worth of raw flash capacity is going. Straight into one of these rack cabinets, where it can be used for all sorts of AI-related purposes. The sometimes-intelligent beast needs feeding, and Kioxia and Dell appear to have worked very hard to fit its lunch inside one handy box.

articles.headline: Is Jensen Huang’s bad behavior more commonplace than it seems?
keyFacts: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faced a recent scandal, but industry experts say executive misconduct and espionage risks are widespread.
Nate Singer of Heron Intelligence stated that state-sponsored actors are embedded in companies and target vulnerable executives.
Semiconductor companies have long been targets for trade secret theft, with multiple prosecutions occurring over the past two decades.
body: The AI industry is still reeling from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s honeypot scandal, but some in the industry see it as an issue that’s much larger than one man.

The Chinese government has been active in economic espionage for decades, and with semiconductors at the center of the AI boom, there’s intense pressure to infiltrate any company involved. At the same time, many of the executives getting rich off that boom have made themselves easy targets.

As CEO of investment intel firm Heron Intelligence, Nate Singer has a unique view into the problem. His firm works on corporate due diligence: Essentially, making sure companies know the relevant dirt before making a major acquisition or executive hire. And while the Nvidia case is particularly severe, Singer says it’s just the tip of the iceberg.
“We’ve got former employees talking about behavior at senior executive levels,” Singer told TechCrunch, saying executives are “really crossing lines that should not be crossed.”

In a widely circulated LinkedIn post, Singer detailed one case in which a CEO’s wife made an unexpected board room appearance, “screaming about her husband and another company exec flying around in the corporate jet with a couple young ladies (who also turned out to be state-sponsored actors).”
It’s an alarming story, but an unfortunately common one. Singer says he’s seen at least three reports of similar cases, and suspects many more have gone unreported.
“There’s a lot more than this one woman,” Singer said. “They are embedded in these companies.”

Semiconductor companies are already big targets for international trade secret theft. There have been dozens of prosecutions for similar cases in recent years, including a case involving the fabrication powerhouse TSMC in 2006.

In 2017, four executives at an unnamed “Bay Area semiconductor equipment manufacturer” were charged with stealing trade secrets for use at a competing company in China. According to the indictment, the technology in question “related to the high-volume manufacturing of semiconductor wafers to be used in lighting and electronic devices, such as flat screen televisions and smart phones.“

Any sexual elements in such cases rarely become public, in part because of the severe consequences for executives and their companies. But according to Singer, the ongoing threat has become a kind of open secret in the industry.
“There are a lot of senior people in the industry that know this is happening, and are effectively condoning it,” he told TechCrunch.

articles.headline: Probably Stolen Cadet Serpico quest walkthrough: All choices and endings
keyFacts: Cadet Serpico's quest in Probably Stolen begins automatically after his initial store visits and involves a bribery scandal.
Players must deliver 2,000 kg of food to the Dumping Ground to prevent Serpico from dying during the quest.
The quest concludes with three possible endings depending on whether players help Serpico join the Revolution, the Black Market, or the Security force.
body: Among the wide array of NPCs you can meet in Probably Stolen , Cadet Serpico makes an impression as a fresh-out-of-the-academy idealist, looking to clean up corruption from the inside.
But as we all know, the space station is not a kind place for someone with bright eyes. Here’s a step-by-step guide on Cadet Serpico’s quest on Probably Stole n , including all possible endings.
Probably Stolen Cadet Serpico quest walkthrough

Much like Eleanor’s , Serpico’s quest starts after his first visit to the store. He usually appears within the fourth to sixth week, although I had multiple runs where he failed to make an appearance at all. There’s no need to sell him anything during his first visits, as his quest will progress automatically no matter what.

Screenshot by Destructoid On his third visit, the gears will start to move after he reports a bribery scandal to his commanding officer. That causes a different officer to visit the store a few days later, claiming Serpico is corrupt and placing a bounty of 300 Credits on his head.

Screenshot by Destructoid The cadet then visits the store the following day, explaining the situation before disappearing. You will hear from him next from Georgio, who comes in bringing a letter. In it, Serpico asks for your help, which you can provide by dropping off 2,000 kg of food at the Dumping Ground within the next three days.

You can either deliver the food yourself or accept Georgio’s proposition and let him take care of it for 150 Credits. Just keep in mind that Georgio will only make the offer if you have over 40 Rep with the Lower Levels. Failing to deliver the food or ignoring the letter will cause Serpico to die.

Screenshot by Destructoid Upon helping Serpico survive, a Security Officer will stop by again, raising his bounty to 600 Credits. Following that, Serpico visits in around a week and asks for your opinion on what he should do with his findings. This sets up the quest’s final major choice and ending. You can check out each decision’s outcome below:

[Revolution] Hand it to the Revolution : Serpico gives his findings to the Revolution, who makes it public. He joins them, now resolved to clean the system, and leaves you with a choice gift between 1x Storage Bay [Extended], 4x Module Expansion Kits, and 2x Current Converters.
[ Black Market] Sell it and escape : Serpico heads to the Black Market. Later on, you receive a sum of Credits and the notice of his death.

[Security] Hand it to a trusting higher-ranking officer : This is only available if you have +50 Rep with Security. Serpico gives his findings to a trusted officer and is promoted to an anti-corruption squad. He visits the store one more time, offering the same rewards available in the Revolution ending.
Screenshot by Destructoid Now that you know how to guide Serpico in the right direction, make sure to also check out how to buy the store in Probably Stolen .

articles.headline: Top four teams in Fifa rankings set to be kept apart until semi-finals at 2027 Women’s World Cup
keyFacts: Fifa confirmed the top four ranked teams will be separated until the semi-finals at the 2027 Women’s World Cup.
Seedings for the tournament will be based on the world rankings updated on 7 December.
The official draw for the 32-team tournament will take place on 11 December in Rio de Janeiro.
body: The top four-ranked teams will be separated until the semi-finals at the 2027 Women’s World Cup, provided they each win their group, after a change to the tournament’s draw procedure was confirmed by Fifa.

Spain, the United States, Germany and England are currently ranked one to four in the world respectively, although the US and England still need to qualify for the tournament. The seedings will be based on 7 December’s updated rankings, meaning the standings could change before the draw, which will take place on 11 December in Rio de Janeiro.

The top four sides were also separated until the semi-finals of the 2026 men’s World Cup, which consisted of 48 teams, but it was not announced until Wednesday that the same rule would apply to the 32-team women’s tournament. In the men’s World Cup the top four – Spain, Argentina, France and England – all reached the semi-finals.

Record four-time champions the US face El Salvador on 27 November as they bid to confirm their place at next summer’s tournament. A victory, coupled with no changes to the world rankings, would ensure the Americans would be placed in the opposite half of the draw to the defending champions, Spain. That would mean if they win their groups the two teams could not meet until the final, which will be played at the Maracanã Stadium on 25 July. Neither Spain nor the US finished top of their group at the last World Cup.

England, the 2023 runners-up, must beat Ukraine over two legs on 1 and 5 December to ensure their qualification. The European champions hold a healthy 31-point advantage over fifth-placed Japan in the world rankings before the upcoming round of internationals.

France, the hosts Brazil and Sweden – who finished third at three of the past four World Cups, and face Scotland in their qualifying playoff in December – would complete the set of eight Pot 1 seeds for the eight groups, if the current top eight remains as it is. Canada, ranked ninth in the world, could pounce on a Pot 1 spot if anyone slips up.

Fifa have also confirmed that the draw will take place at 1.30pm local time (11.30am EST/4.30pm GMT) on 11 December, at Rio de Janeiro’s Museum of Modern Art. Brazil, as hosts, will be placed into Group A and will contest the opening match at the Maracanã on 24 June.

After the eight Pot 1 sides, the next eight highest-ranked teams involved will be in Pot 2, with the next eight below them in Pot 3. Pot 4 will include three places for the winners of the inter-confederation playoff tournament that will conclude in March, along with the lowest-ranked sides involved.
No group will be permitted to include more than one team from the same continent, except for European teams, of whom there can be a maximum of two per group.

articles.headline: Pochettino ready to accept Man Utd offer to replace Carrick
keyFacts: Mauricio Pochettino is prepared to accept an offer to become the next head coach of Manchester United.
United officials are meeting to decide the future of current head coach Michael Carrick, who is expected to be relieved of his duties.
Manchester United would be required to pay a $10 million release fee to sign Pochettino from his current contract with US Soccer.
body: - Published
Mauricio Pochettino is ready to accept an offer from Manchester United to become their next head coach.
United have opened talks with the Argentine about him potentially replacing Michael Carrick, who is expected to be relieved of his duties in the next 48 hours.
Once Carrick's future is clarified, sources have told BBC Sport that USA manager Pochettino wants to take the job.
US Soccer officials are expecting an official approach from United - and sources have told BBC Sport they have a contingency plan for their manager leaving, which includes a succession plan.
Former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino wants to remain respectful to the US Soccer Federation and will wait for United to make their approach.
The Red Devils would be required to pay $10m (Â£7.5m) to release Pochettino from his contract, which he only signed in August.
The USA have a two-legged Concacaf Nations League quarter-final against Haiti over the next week.
With confidence over a succession plan, it raises the possibility that Pochettino may not take charge of those games.
On Thursday, US Soccer cancelled planned media with players citing a clash with Veterans Day, though some reports claimed it was to stop the squad being asked about their manager.
Pochettino, 54, is understood to view the prospect of managing United as a serious opportunity, with the expectation being he would accept the job were it formally offered.

United have spoken to the ex-Argentina defender about their managerial position on three previous occasions - when Jose Mourinho was sacked in 2018, then in 2022 before the club appointed Erik ten Hag and again when the Dutchman was sacked in 2024.
Carrick's future at United will be decided at a meeting in Monaco on Wednesday that will be attended by chief executive Omar Berrada, director of football Jason Wilcox and co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe.
Berrada and Wilcox have flown to Monaco for one of their regular, planned meetings to discuss strategy around the football club.
On this occasion, the main issue to be decided is Carrick's future and what should happen next.
It is expected that Berrada and Wilcox's recommendation is for the head coach to go.
Carrick, 45, was pictured arriving at the club's Carrington training base on Wednesday.
United are 18th in the Premier League - inside the relegation zone - after winning just one of their first 10 games and none since August.
It is the club's lowest position at this stage of a top-flight season since 1986-87, when they were 20th.
Pochettino's first job in the Premier League was at Southampton from January 2013, before a five-year stint at Tottenham from 2014 that included a Champions League final appearance.
He managed Paris St-Germain from January 2021 to July 2022 before spending the 2023-24 season in charge of Chelsea.
Pochettino moved into international football by taking the USA job in September 2024, and led the co-hosts to the last 16 of the 2026 World Cup.
Analysis: More clarity on Carrick future expected today

While it may seem a touch immoral for Manchester United to be talking to a potential new manager before they have decided if their current one is staying or not, this kind of situation is not uncommon in football.

Jose Mourinho had agreed a contract with United in 2016 before Louis van Gaal was sacked, which is how stories - including from BBC Sport - came out that the Dutchman would be dismissed as he was celebrating the FA Cup final triumph over Crystal Palace.
Going further back, Mark Hughes was replaced immediately by Roberto Mancini at Manchester City in 2009. Hughes' imminent dismissal was reported on the morning of his final game in charge.

It is impossible to reach that situation without talks taking place beforehand, and it would be naive to think they do not go on in a world in which agents are pushing clients for jobs that either do, or do not, exist or clubs are trying to gauge interest before making a decision.

I have been told by one source the Pochettino terms to join United are more or less agreed. I have also been told if they decide to push on, United can decide whether the former Spurs and Chelsea boss remains with the USA team for their matches against Haiti.

If he did stay, it would mean a sharp turnaround from a Tuesday night match - which finishes in the early hours of Wednesday - to be at Carrington for preparations before United's game against Liverpool at Anfield on 22 November.
There are a lot of gaps to fill in yet, not least whether Carrick will be dismissed or not.
But it seems more likely there will be clarity on that on Wednesday, and from that the rest of the jigsaw pieces should start to slot into place.

articles.headline: Tekken Boss Katsuhiro Harada Says Developing For Xbox Series S ‘Feels Like Having To Do Extra Work For A Slightly Weaker Child’
keyFacts: Tekken producer Katsuhiro Harada criticized the Xbox Series S, stating that developing for the console requires extra work due to its lower performance.
CD Projekt Red associate game director Paweł Sasko noted that while the console presents optimization challenges, its lower price helps developers reach more players.
Harada expressed concern that Microsoft might release a similar lower-performance console for the next generation based on the current model's popularity.
body: Recently, a group of five storied game developers lined up onstage in Seoul to be interviewed by former Sony indie head Shuhei Yoshida about their work, particularly as it relates to console games. And as part of that discussion, Tekken producer Katsuhiro Harada made a very deliberate point to call out the Xbox Series S for being a pain to develop games for.

As reported and translated by Inven Global, the interview was moderated by Yoshida and included Harada; DongKi Lee, the CTO of Stellar Blade studio ShiftUp;Â Danganronpa head Kazutaka Kodaka; CDPR associate game director PaweÅ Sasko; and Tynan Sylvester, CEO of Rimworld maker Ludeon Studios. Harada’s remarks were precipitated by the question of what advantages and disadvantages there were to developing for console as opposed to PC. Initially, Harada talked about the advantage of consoles in esports tournaments for fighting games like Tekken. But then, he took a moment to share a very particular opinion:

That said, there’s something I really want to say while I have the floor. Since a senior Xbox official is actually in attendance here today, I wish hardware like the “Xbox Series S” wouldn’t be released (laughs). I want to ask Director PaweÅ personallyâhonestly, weren’t you upset inside because of Series S?
Sasko was careful in his initial response, laughing and saying it “constantly throws challenges at us and forces us to optimize our code very cleanly.” But Harada wasn’t done:

You just used a very polite and elegant way to say “Xbox Series S sucks,” right? (laughs) Low memory is an issue, but the hardest part is that it’s a device so similar to Series X while having awkwardly lower performance. When porting to Switch 2, developers can shift their mindset to “Switch 2 is a distinct device for Nintendo fans!” But with Xbox, after delivering your absolute best output, it feels like having to do extra work for a slightly weaker child.

Furthermore, in markets like the U.S., there are more Series S users than Series X users, so we can’t just cut corners. Yet after launch, Series S users direct their complaints at us developers rather than Microsoft, asking “Why is texture resolution lower only on Series S?”

This time, Sasko gave a more detailed response, though he still shared a much more optimistic view than Harada did, ultimately landing on praising the Series S for the way its lower price enables developers to reach more players:

Harada speaks a lot of truth. Players don’t fully understand the technical context behind why fewer characters appear on screen or why visuals are downgraded. However, intensely optimizing for lower-spec platforms definitely brings the benefit of making the game run significantly better across all platformsâincluding PS5, high-end PCs, and handhelds like Steam Deck and ROG Ally. Recently, with Cyberpunk 2077 Version 2.5, we applied optimization breakthroughs gained while preparing the Switch 2 launch title (which involved a team of 80 to 100 people for over a year) back to all other platforms with great effect.

And the biggest advantage of Series S is that its affordable price makes it accessible. Not every gamer can buy expensive high-end hardware, so from a developer’s perspective, even if the strict constraints are painful, there is a silver lining in expanding market penetration to deliver the game to more players.

Harada wasn’t having it, concluding by noting that Sasko “packaged Series S so gracefully that the Microsoft representative in the audience keeps nodding along. I’m worried they’ll feel reassured and release a successor like ‘Helix S’ for the next-gen Xbox as well.”

It’s no longer a secret that some developers are chafing at having to make games compatible with the weaker Series S console. Baldur’s Gate 3‘s struggles to release on the platform due to issues with splitscreen co-op were the first major sign that something was amiss here, though even before that some developers were reportedly quietly complaining about Xbox’s requirements that games be compatible with both. More recently, Funcom chief product officer Scott Junior said it was a “challenge” to get Dune Awakening on Series S (it did eventually release on the console), and Moon Studio head Thomas Mahler blamed the Series S for No Rest for the Wicked‘s delayed release on Xbox. Also, curiously, Stellar Blade was announced for Xbox but still hasn’t made it to the console. Lee didn’t comment on this in the interview, and it’s unknown if this is related to issues with porting the game to Series S or to any number of other possible reasons.

Part of the trouble, as Sasko mentions, is that the Xbox Series S has historically been popular relative to the X, at least in the early stages of the console generation and thanks to lower availability of the X. Xbox Series S initially led Xbox console sales over the X for several years post-launchâas of 2022 it made up nearly 75 percent of the share of Series consoles sold. In the following year, that gap began to close, and by 2024 the X had outsold the S, at least in the U.S. It isn’t yet clear if rising console prices across the board will serve to bring the Series S back in vogue relative to its larger sibling, though its current price of $200 more than it originally retailed for may have something to do with the constant decline of Xbox console sales (Xbox blames supply constraints).

articles.headline: Ranchers want a jury. Washington state offers a board
keyFacts: Washington's Department of Ecology fined ranchers Wade and Teresa King $267,540, claiming the couple damaged protected wetlands.
The Kings dispute the penalty and requested a jury trial, but state officials argue the ranchers have no right to a jury.
The Kings' lawyers said they will ask the U.S. Supreme Court to intervene if Washington courts deny their jury trial request.
body: Wade and Teresa King run cattle on ground their family has worked since the 1950s. In February 2023, Washington state’s Department of Ecology fined them $267,540. The state claims the Kings dug up protected wetlands. The Kings say they just maintained stockwater ponds, which ranchers in dry country have to do. Somebody must decide who’s right, and the Kings want a jury to do it.

I’m a husband and father of three who runs a small business and has coached youth teams for years. Coaching teaches you fast that nobody accepts a call from someone with a stake in the score. Thirty years in finance, including expert witness work in securities and fiduciary cases, taught me the adult version: the side with better evidence welcomes outside judgment. My argument is short. When a state seeks to punish, citizens should decide the facts.

Ecology tells the story differently. It says the original penalty covered at least 23 alkali wetlands, about 6.37 acres, with 18 on state-leased land, two on federal land, and three on the Kings’ own. It relied on aerial photographs back to 1949, site inspections, and soil and water tests. The Kings dispute its conclusion, and the $3.7 million compliance figure comes from their own lawyers. Nobody has tested either account in front of a neutral factfinder.

A Grant County judge dismissed the Kings’ suit in August without ruling on the jury right. In September, an appeals commissioner paused the board proceeding while the appeal continues. As of November 2026, I can’t find a ruling on whether the Kings get a jury.

The founders built the jury to keep government honest. Thomas Jefferson called it “the only anchor, ever yet imagined by man” for holding a government to its constitution. Washington’s Constitution says the right “shall remain inviolate,” and courts measure it against what juries did in 1889. In 1989 the state Supreme Court struck down a cap on jury damage awards on that basis in Sofie v. Fibreboard . That’s the deal: government gets the power to punish, and citizens keep the final say on the facts.

Federal law points the same direction. In SEC v. Jarkesy in 2024, six justices held that when the Securities and Exchange Commission seeks civil penalties for securities fraud, the Seventh Amendment guarantees a jury, because penalties meant to punish are a remedy courts have traditionally imposed. That ruling binds federal agencies. It doesn’t bind Washington, since a 1916 decision holds the Seventh Amendment doesn’t apply to the states. In October 2025, Justice Neil Gorsuch agreed that the decision is “something of a relic” and urged the court to revisit it. The Kings’ lawyers say they’ll ask the justices to do so if Washington’s courts turn them down.

I don’t see a villain here. The legislature created the Pollution Control Hearings Board to provide a “more expeditious and efficient” way to resolve environmental appeals. Its three members are appointed by the governor, and the board is unaffiliated with the Ecology Department. A six-figure penalty calls for more deliberation than efficiency allows. The jury guarantee dates to 1889. The hearing board was created in 1970. (Hollywood made 12 Angry Men in 1957. Nobody has pitched “Three Appointees Deliberate.”)

To be sure, the state has a fair argument. Wetland disputes turn on soil chemistry and hydrology, and a board that hears them daily may handle them better than a jury that hears one. The attorney general’s office says the Kings have no jury right, and Jarkesy itself left agencies room to act without juries in areas like customs and public benefits. The Kings expect the Ecology Department to argue the penalty is incidental to its restoration orders, and they cite the department’s own filing calling the two distinct. The state could win these points. Even so, expertise argues for calling expert witnesses, which juries hear every day. If the Ecology Department’s evidence is as strong as the state says, a jury will find for it, and the Kings will have lost to their neighbors instead of an agency, a result both sides could respect.
CONGRESS CAN’T REFEREE ITSELF

Washington state can fix this in stages. Its courts should apply Article 1, Section 21 the way Sofie did and send punitive penalties to a jury. If they won’t, the legislature can let anyone facing a large civil penalty move the case to superior court and a jury, a change that needs no constitutional ruling. And the U.S. Supreme Court should take a case that lets it revisit Bombolis , so a citizen’s jury right doesn’t change at the state line. I’ll answer my next jury summons without a sigh, and I’d suggest you do the same.

Aldo Leopold asked Americans to see land as “a community to which we belong.” The Ecology Department says it’s protecting rare wetlands. The Kings say they’re keeping water available for cattle, which is its own kind of stewardship. This country has an old way to resolve a dispute between neighbors over facts: hand it to a jury of other neighbors. Wade and Teresa King have asked for that. Let a jury decide whether the ponds are wetlands.

Jay Rogers is a financial professional with more than 30 years of experience in private equity, private credit, hedge funds, and wealth management. He writes about issues in finance, constitutional law, national security, human nature, and public policy.

articles.headline: Has the torch passed to a really new generation of Americans?
keyFacts: The 2026 midterm results included notable Democratic victories, such as James Talarico winning a Texas Senate seat and Abdul el Sayed securing a Michigan Senate seat.
Author Kim Ezra Shienbaum stated that the election outcomes reflect a new generation of voters prioritizing entitlements and adopting anti-Western ideologies cultivated in universities.
Shienbaum claimed that decades of institutional transformations in higher education, including foreign funding and Marxist-inspired curricula, contributed to this political shift.
body: Ordinary Americans, politicians, and pundits alike continue to ponder the unexpected, even astonishing, 2026 midterm results. Among the most striking outcomes: a Texas Senate seat flipped blue by James Talarico , a seminarian who once stated, “ God is nonbinary ”; Michigan’s Senate seat secured by a pugnacious Abdul el Sayed, whose victory speech to Michiganders opened in Arabic and whose campaign kept deeply polarizing company; and a House seat won by CUNY graduate student Darializa Avila Chevalier, known for her explicit and vulgar anti-American rhetoric.

It’s time to ask whether John F. Kennedy’s iconic call to civic duty — “Ask not what your country can do for you; ask what you can do for your country” — still has an audience among young people raised on grievance and entitlement.

In the midterm elections, this more diverse generation flipped the Kennedy script, demanding instead what their government could do for them. Electorates chose candidates offering a tempting assortment of taxpayer-funded entitlements. Affordability crises were aggressively linked to capitalism by socialist candidates, while el Sayed audaciously tied high domestic grocery costs to foreign aid for Israel — messaging amplified by a Rebellion PAC advertisement that crossed the line into unabashed antisemitism.

While high inflation, anti-war sentiment, and Trump fatigue have been blamed for this sweeping Democratic victory, an accurate postmortem requires digging deeper — straight into institutional transformations that began in the 1960s.

As a college professor who has spent decades watching the internal machinery of higher education evolve, I have seen these ideological seeds being planted firsthand. Following the SDS anti-war protests of the 1960s, the revolutionary spirit disappeared “underground” — hidden in plain sight right inside our universities and the media. New generations of America’s best and brightest came of age in a multiethnic and multicultural nation quietly shaped by imported Marxist academics. They impregnated the social studies, even English departments, with brand new concepts explicitly critical of U.S. history, culture, and values. Meanwhile, the organizational structure of universities permitted one-sided “Studies” departments to exist in plain sight, operating right alongside traditional departments which, at least for a time, still hired faculty with diverse opinions.

Then came the money trail. In the 1990s, and accelerating sharply in the first decade of the 21st century, universities seeking to augment their dwindling coffers welcomed foreign students primarily from the Middle East. These new entrants brought with them the narratives and the prejudices of their home countries, particularly toward the existence of Israel. More concerning, Qatar, the sole Gulf nation aligned with the Muslim Brotherhood, was allowed to inject billions into U.S. education. That funding played a critical role in embedding Muslim postcolonial narratives not only into universities, via the creation of Middle East departments, but also into K-12 school curricula.

It did not take long for Marxist-inspired campus progressives to establish intersectional alliances with newly established chapters of Students for Justice in Palestine, an organization with an explicit political agenda folded in with traditional campus affinity groups. It was the brainchild of Hatem Bazian, who had co-founded American Muslims for Palestine, a group aligned with anti-Zionist, pro-Hamas positions.
EVANGELICAL VOTERS LEFT THEIR DISCERNMENT IN 2022

This convergence successfully fused domestic grievances with foreign agendas, standardizing an anti-Western, anti-Zionist orthodoxy among the student body. As these students graduated and entered the electorate, the radical theories cultivated on campus matured into an aggressive political reality. The Democratic Socialists of America, combining socialism with an explicit anti-Israel core is the result. Eight of its members won in the midterm elections.

The torch has indeed passed to a new generation of Americans, but it is no longer the flame of Kennedy’s civic duty; it is a radical fire explicitly lit to consume the very foundations of the country they were asked to serve.

Kim Ezra Shienbaum, Ph.D., is professor emerita of political science at Rutgers-Camden and author of several books including Beyond Jihad: Critical Voices From Inside Islam (contributing editor with Jamal Hasan, Academica Press, 2006).

articles.headline: Google’s Tabletop AI experiment lets you build custom collaboration apps
keyFacts: Google introduced an experimental AI tool named Tabletop that creates custom collaborative hubs for personal planning.
Google Labs design and engineering lead Roman Nurik stated users can prompt the tool or use templates to generate interactive spaces for groups.
Access to the Tabletop beta is currently rolling out via a waitlist for US residents over the age of 18.
body: Google has cooked up a new experimental AI tool called Tabletop that generates customized collaborative hubs to help you coordinate with family, and friends. The Tabletop platform shares some visual similarities with workplace management apps like Asana and Monday, but with a built-in AI feature that allows you to vibecode personalized interactive tools by describing them, such as savings trackers, chore charts, event plans, and more.
Google’s Tabletop AI experiment lets you build custom collaboration apps
Tabletop provides customizable, collaborative spaces for all your personal planning needs.

“Just add in your links, files and ideas, then prompt @tabletop — or pick a starter template — to generate custom interactive trip itineraries, dinner polls, expense splitters and tournament brackets,” Google Labs design and engineering lead Roman Nurik said in the blog post. “Once your space is ready, drop the invite link in your group chat to let everyone jump in and use it at the same time like a Google Doc.”

Access to the Tabletop beta is rolling out via a waitlist, and currently limited to people over the age of 18 in the US. Some of the example use cases that Nurik provides in his video above would clearly require giving kids or teens access to Tabletop, however, and using this for personal family planning looks like a compelling alternative to stuffy workplace software, so that age requirement might only be in place while Tabletop is in public testing.

articles.headline: There were 47 graphics chip makers in 1998. Where did they all go?
keyFacts: The PC graphics market shrank from 47 companies in 1998 to just two, Nvidia and ATI, within a few years.
Companies failed because they could not keep pace with rapid chip release cycles, rising design costs, or the dot-com crash.
Nvidia currently dominates the market, while Intel's recent attempts to compete have struggled to gain significant market share.
body: Some may find this hard to believe, given the absolute state of the market today, but if you were building a gaming PC in 1998, the hard part wasn’t finding somewhere that had 3D cards in stock for a reasonable price. It was choosing the right one among a glut of potential, reasonably affordable options.

In 1998, 47 companies were designing or selling PC graphics, driving a market that hit 130 million units and outsold PCs themselves. Just two years later, at the turn of the new millennium, only 15 remained, and not long after that, there were merely two: Nvidia and ATI, nowadays part of AMD.

But the Nvidia of the late 1990s and early 2000s was a far cry from the vast (if tarnished) juggernaut it is today, and at the time it wasn’t even the obvious survivor. Research firm 4th Wave put ATI top for 1998 with 24.5 million 3D chips sold, followed by S3 with 15.2 million and Intel, in its first year in the market, with 6.5 million. Nvidia came fourth on 6.4 million. 3dfx, the company whose Voodoo cards had made 3D gaming on PC a thing in the first place, sold 5.2 million.

Each of those companies went under or sold up for one reason or another, but what’s striking is how most did so within a few years of one another. In the four years between 1998 and 2002, the graphics business essentially stopped rewarding whoever had the fastest chip, instead favouring the companies that could iterate the fastest. A new chip every six months or so for the same APIs everyone used, backed by enough capital to ride out the dot-com crash. Nvidia was built for that; almost nobody else was.

The first companies to go didn’t need any help from Nvidia, though. 3D acceleration had made the humble graphics chip a much bigger and more expensive thing to design, and plenty of incumbents that had found their footing on 2D couldn’t afford to keep going. Tseng Labs stopped developing graphics chips at the end of 1997 with roughly $28 million still in the bank, selling its graphics engineers to ATI for about $3 million. Rendition, maker of the Vérité V1000 3D accelerator, agreed to sell itself to memory maker Micron in June 1998, and ATI bought Chromatic Research for $67 million that October.

In its prospectus for its January 1999 IPO, Nvidia warned that PC makers brought out new systems as often as twice a year, on a spring and fall schedule, and that missing one was a serious risk. The company subsequently reorganised itself around that schedule, releasing the GeForce 256 in October 1999 and the GeForce 3 in February 2001. By 2002, Nvidia’s annual report disclosed that separate design teams were working on several generations of chips at once.

By this point, though, the writing had been on the wall for quite some time. S3, then the world’s second-largest graphics chip maker, wrote in its annual report for 1999 that a graphics chip stayed on sale for 12 to 18 months, and that a delay "as short as a few months" could cost it a design win with a PC maker. Any company that was rolling out just one major chip per year was launching against a rival’s refresh at best. At worst, it was launching late against next-gen chips.

That’s essentially what happened to 3dfx when Rampage, the chip that was meant to succeed the Voodoo5, never shipped. The company lost its other big advantage around the same time with Glide, its own programming interface that only ran on Voodoo cards. Glide flourished while Direct3D, Microsoft’s rival interface built into Windows, was still lacking features, meaning that plenty of games ran best on 3dfx hardware, but that lead was quickly eroded once Direct3D and rivals’ OpenGL drivers caught up; developers could now write a game once and run it on anyone’s card. By 1999, Creative was selling Nvidia-based Riva TNT cards with drivers that let Glide games run on them. 3dfx sued, then open-sourced Glide altogether that December.

By then, though, 3dfx had already made its most damaging mistake. A year earlier, on December 14, 1998, it agreed to buy graphics card maker STB Systems for about $141 million in stock, and CEO Greg Ballard said the Voodoo3 would only be sold on 3dfx’s cards. That revelation left Diamond and Creative in a tough spot, having built their gaming lines on Voodoo chips. They were now stuck high and dry without access to the new one.

3dfx was solely concerned with its margins here. The price of its single-chip Voodoo Banshee card dropped from $150 to $89 within a month of launch. With prices in freefall, selling the finished Voodoo Banshee meant that 3dfx pocketed the margin that’d otherwise go to a partner like Diamond or Creative. Those boardmakers inevitably walked, and went where the chips were. STB had been selling Nvidia cards right up to the deal, and its last annual report includes a $3 million note it held from "Nvidia Corporation, a supplier." Creative already had Riva TNT cards on shelves, and Nvidia, which then didn’t make its own cards, would sell its chips to anyone.

Intel, meanwhile, was causing problems from the other end of the market. Its i740 "Auburn" graphics chip launched in early 1998, and Microprocessor Report, the newsletter for the industry’s engineers, argued that Intel’s arrival encouraged Cirrus Logic, Oak and others to fold that year. Just over a year later, after lacklustre sales, Intel confirmed that it was ending support for the i740, then pulled out of standalone desktop graphics chips altogether to put graphics into its motherboard chipsets instead, starting with the i810. This was extremely problematic for companies like S3, Trident, and SiS. They survived on cheap chips for big PC makers, and by the second half of 2001, estimates say Intel’s integrated graphics business had risen to control 55% of the market. That, in turn, pushed S3 to sell its graphics business to a VIA joint venture for $323 million.

Then the money ran out. Venture funding for graphics startups had already dried up in 1999 as the dot-com bubble deflated, and exits inevitably followed. 3dfx lost $100.5 million in the second quarter of 2000, with its CEO blaming a late Voodoo5, and on December 15 that year it sold its assets to Nvidia for $70 million in cash (and a million Nvidia shares) after failing to secure credit. STMicroelectronics, which made the PowerVR-based Kyro II, quit PC graphics in early 2002.

ATI, however, survived alongside Nvidia because it was already operating in the way the new market wanted it to. It was the biggest seller at the time, and it made its own graphics cards, which Microprocessor Report said brought in most of its revenue and margin. So, making its own cards wasn’t 3dfx’s mistake; it was locking out boardmakers who had been selling Voodoo cards for it. That pushed those boardmakers towards Nvidia, and a late Voodoo5 and cash crunch dealt the death blow. ATI also used its stock to buy the engineers that its rivals were shedding: Tseng’s, Chromatic’s, then, in February 2000, ArtX’s for $400 million, a team that’d just designed the Flipper graphics chip for Nintendo’s GameCube.

For the next two decades, the the graphics industry was dominated by ATI - which eventually folded into AMD in 2006 - and Nvidia. For a while, it was a real fight. AMD paid $5.4 billion for ATI, and in the second quarter of 2010, Radeon cards briefly overtook Nvidia in discrete graphics shipments. However, AMD had a problem: it couldn’t really afford ATI. It wrote off $1.6 billion of goodwill from the deal about a year after it closed, and its PC chip business kept struggling.

By early 2015, AMD’s CPU and GPU revenue was down 38% on the year, and the company was close to negative book value. Its quarterly R&D budget had fallen to its lowest level since 2004, with Nvidia spending nearly half as much again. Radeon cards stayed on the same Graphics Core Next architecture for about seven years before RDNA arrived in 2019. By then, Nvidia had already launched its RTX cards with dedicated ray tracing hardware and Tensor cores for AI, and it never gave that lead back.

Intel was the only company with pockets deep enough to try breaking back in. Its first go, Larrabee, was cancelled as a consumer graphics chip in December 2009. It finally got there in 2022, when the Arc A770 went on sale from $329, alongside the cheaper A750. Both arrived after repeated delays and struggled with older DirectX 9 games, and many observers - RPS included - put their chances of breaking up the Nvidia-AMD duopoly at low. By the time then-hardware editor James returned to the A750 in 2023, Intel had drastically improved its drivers, bringing big gains to both general performance and DX9 compatibility. Even then, the Arc series had yet to prove it could work well at launch, without the need to be ironed out across months of updates.

The second generation did indeed fare better, with the Arc B580 successfully selling out at $249 in December 2024. But that still barely impacted the wider industry, with Intel sitting at just 1% of graphics card shipments in the third quarter of 2025 and around 2% this spring, when Nvidia took roughly 90% of the 12.5 million cards shipped.

It now looks like Intel is on its way back out of gaming graphics cards. In April, leaker Jaykihn claimed that its next-generation Celestial gaming cards had been cancelled "long ago," and the latest rumours say B580 supply could be cut so Intel can sell more Arc Pro cards for, surprise surprise, AI work. It’s important to note that Intel hasn’t confirmed any of that, and one of its execs has said that Arc isn’t leaving its PC roadmap. Still, Intel had everything 3dfx didn’t: the cash, the PC makers on side, and the same APIs as everyone else. But money can’t buy two decades of Nvidia and AMD fixing their drivers game by game, and it seems to have decided its capital is better spent on AI anyway.

Evidently, the question of where all the other GPU makers went does not have one single answer. Some couldn’t afford the rising costs, some couldn’t keep pace with a new Nvidia chip every six months, and some lost their cheap business to Intel’s integrated graphics or went under when the dot-com bubble burst. Left over was a Nvidia/ATI (later AMD) duopoly, and PC gamers haven’t exactly done well out of it. We saw the RTX 4080 launch at $1,199 in 2022, nearly twice the 3080’s price, and the ongoing, AI-driven RAM shortage has pushed prices higher still.

In 1998, 47 companies wanted your money. Now there are two, and the bigger one, Nvidia, sells nine of every 10 graphics cards - yet still makes most of its money from data centres. Eighteen years on, it's a bad time to be a PC gamer, and nobody’s in a hurry to make things any better.

articles.headline: Iran vows not to give up "a single particle" of nuclear material
keyFacts: An Iranian official said Tehran will not remove any enriched nuclear material, rejecting a U.S. condition for a peace deal.
Insurer Allianz Trade said war damage will cost Persian Gulf nations over $200 billion, with losses reaching $790 billion by 2030.
Iran rejected U.S. claims that 80 percent of its nuclear base was destroyed, stating its weapons stockpile exceeds American estimates.
body: What to know about the Iran war today:

- The head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council vowed Wednesday that Tehran would not allow the removal of "even a single particle of enriched nuclear material" from the country, casting doubt on diplomatic efforts as the U.S. has long sought a peace deal that would see Iran give up its enriched uranium.

- President Trump has argued that he needed to launch the to prevent the Islamic Republic from obtaining a nuclear weapon, which the regime has always denied any intention of doing. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth told reporters Tuesday that "crazy Islamists in Tehran will never ever have a nuclear weapon."

- The war with Iran will cost Persian Gulf nations, most of which are close U.S. allies, more than $200 billion in damages, insurer Allianz Trade said Wednesday. Economic losses could reach nearly four times that amount by 2030, the insurer added.
3 missiles from Iran-backed Houthis intercepted, Saudi-led coalition says
The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said on Wednesday that it shot down three cruise missiles fired at Riyadh, which has been targeted for weeks by the Iran-backed group.
"Air defenses intercepted and destroyed 3 cruise missiles launched by the Houthi terrorist militia toward the Riyadh area," coalition spokesperson Turki al-Malki posted on social media.
The latest incident comes after the Houthis damaged a skyscraper belonging to oil giant Saudi Aramco in the capital's gleaming financial district on Sunday.
Riyadh's international airport has also been targeted repeatedly, with deadly attacks forcing it to close for two weeks last month.
Saudi Arabia formed an international coalition to fight the Houthis in 2015, after the group's takeover of Yemen's capital Sanaa.
After years of an uneasy truce, the conflict reignited in July.
Iranian Defense Ministry rejects "deceptive figures fabricated" by Hegseth on Iran's military capacity

Iran's Defense Ministry on Wednesday rejected Defense Secretary Pete of Tehran's military capacities, calling his depiction a fabrication and insisting Iranian armed forces still had weapons stockpiled.

Iran's weapons stockpile "far exceeds the deceptive figures fabricated by Trump and the defeated Pete," a ministry spokesperson said, adding that the country had made use of "strategic production and upgraded technologies."
Hegseth told reporters Tuesday that during 40 days of combat, the U.S. had struck 13,000 targets, destroying, he said, more than 80% of Iran's nuclear industrial base.
"Their navy sunk, their air force grounded, their defense industrial base gone," Hegseth said.
Iranian officials that the country's weapons production capacity had increased by 250% since the war began, with help from Russia and China.

Neither side has offered evidence to prove their claims, and neither the U.S. nor Iran have launched large-scale strikes since the summer. Both claim to have won the war, but despite Hegseth's assertion on Tuesday that the Strait of Hormuz is under U.S. control, Iran continues attacking vessels daily in and near the waterway.
Bessent relocated to military base after threats from Iran
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has relocated from his home in the Washington, D.C., area to a military base following a series of Iranian threats against his life.

"The secretary will not be deterred by the Iranian regime's threats and remains committed to executing Operation Economic Outcast and maintaining the blockade, which together are collapsing Iran's economy," a Treasury Department spokesperson said.
A source familiar with the situation pointed to a Wall Street Journal story as the impetus for the move.

"After The Wall Street Journal published an article featuring an online photo that allowed the location of the secretary's Georgetown home to be geo-located, security concerns began to increase which have now forced the secretary to relocate to a military base for his safety," the person told CBS News.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian accused the U.S. on Wednesday of threatening to attack his country with America's largest non-nuclear weapon — the "mother of all bombs" — while claiming to seek a diplomatic resolution to the war.
In a post on X, Pezeshkian criticized the U.S. for what he called an effort to "pursue diplomacy through threats."
"No contradiction but a disgrace. Who threatens global peace and security?" he wrote.

CBS News in October that the White House and Pentagon had prepared plans to use the Massive Ordnance Air Blast Bomb, or MOAB — an acronym that has earned it the nickname used by Pezeshkian — to hit military sites in Iran if President Trump were to give the order, according to sources familiar with the matter.

The MOAB is the largest non-nuclear weapon in the U.S. arsenal, weighing upwards of 30,000 pounds. Mr. Trump set a precedent for its use in 2017, when it was deployed to attack an ISIS cave complex in Afghanistan. It is designed to destroy infrastructure buried deep underground.
Iranian official says Europe and the U.S. have "heard the repercussions" of war
An adviser to Iran's supreme leader said Wednesday that the U.S. and Europe "have heard the repercussions" of the war launched jointly more than eight months ago by the U.S. and Israel.
In a post on X, Mohammad Mokhber said other nations' participation in the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports constituted an act of war that would be recorded "in the nation's historical memory."

Iran-linked groups have also been accused of in the U.K. and Europe, including many targeting Jewish communities.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said Wednesday that two more oil tankers had struck sea mines and caught on fire in the Strait of Hormuz, the latest of what have become daily claims by Iranian forces about attacks on commercial vessels in and around the strategic waterway.

"Two oil tankers that attempted to secretly leave the Strait of Hormuz last night via an unauthorized and hazardous route, under the protection of fighter jets belonging to the plundering and aggressor U.S. military, struck naval mines and sustained massive explosions," the IRGC said in a statement.

Iran has attacked ships for months that it accuses of trying to transit the waterway without its approval, using southern shipping lanes the U.S. military insists are safe and open. The U.S. military, meanwhile, has also struck tankers it accuses of violating its blockade of Iranian ports.

The IRGC claimed Tuesday that at least two oil tankers had caught on fire after explosions in the strait under similar circumstances, and the U.K. navy's Maritime Trade Operations center said a tanker reported being hit by a projectile in the strait on Tuesday evening.

"Physical damage across the region is assessed just above $200bn, mostly concentrated in Hormuz-locked economies, especially in energy infrastructure," the insurer said in a report.
More than 80 energy facilities were hit in the war, mostly in Kuwait, Qatar and Bahrain, the report said, with a third of them "severely damaged."
Beyond physical damage to energy infrastructure, the war has affected other sectors like tourism and real estate, which will see slower growth over the years.
"The total cost of the war for the GCC is set to reach $790bn, a cumulative gap of 5.9 percent of GDP relative to the pre-war trend through 2030," the report said.

"This reflects the cumulative loss of economic output over 2026-30, the difference between what the region was forecast to produce on its pre-war growth trend and what it is now projected to produce post-war," it said.

On Tuesday, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth reiterated the White House's position on Iran's nuclear program, telling reporters that "crazy Islamists in Tehran will never ever have a nuclear weapon."
Iranian foreign minister mocks France over being "unable to manage fridges"

Hours after the Iranian foreign ministry officially rejected any responsibility for grocery store refrigerators being hacked across the country, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi added insult to injury.

articles.headline: Chinese researchers set new data records for 'hollow-core' fiber tech
keyFacts: Chinese researchers achieved a record 64Tbps transmission capacity over 1,007 kilometers using hollow-core fiber technology.
Hollow-core fiber uses air instead of solid glass to reduce resistance, resulting in faster data transmission speeds and lower latency.
Scientists are working to overcome manufacturing and installation challenges to make this technology more commercially viable for infrastructure and data centers.
body: - Chinese researchers report major hollow-core fiber upgrades
- Transmission capacities of 64Tbps were reached
- The technology could replace solid-core fiber in infrastructure networks

No matter how fast your broadband (or 5G) connection is, it could always be faster, and 'hollow-core' fiber could help. Researchers in China have now set new records for the technology, demonstrating two-way, high-speed data transmission across a distance of 1,007 kilometers (626 miles).

As reported by CCTV (via Interesting Engineering), a transmission capacity of 64 terabits per second (Tbps) was achieved in each direction, enough to download 160 films in 4K resolution (50GB each) every second — so perfect for movie night. Individual signals took just 3.43 milliseconds to travel the whole length of the link.

The transmission distance is some 50 times greater than previous hollow-core trials of the same type, while latency was reduced by 30%, too. Signal-to-noise ratios and loss margins were also improved, according to the team from the China Telecom Research Institute, Yangtze Optical Fibre and Cable (YOFC), and ZTE Corporation.

It's a technology that companies are already investing in. For example, last year Microsoft signed a deal with Corning and Heraeus to scale up production of hollow-core fiber in order to upgrade its Azure cloud platform. By the end of this year, around 15,000 kilometers (9,321 miles) of hollow-core fiber should be in place supporting Azure.
A core change

As you can guess from the name, hollow-core fiber replaces the glass of solid-core fiber with air that has a glass lattice surrounding it. The glass edges keep optical signals heading in the right direction, but the hollow core means there's less resistance to the light — which results in faster transmission speeds and lower latency.

The technology is better suited to large infrastructure projects than the cabling that connects your broadband network to your home, but you'll still feel the benefit in the coming years: data centers are already making use of the technology, and it's been tipped to support cellular networks too in the future.

Several challenges remain, because hollow-core fiber is more challenging to make and install than solid-core fiber, the current norm. However, as this latest demonstration in China shows, scientists are gradually overcoming some of the problems that remain, making the tech more commercially viable all the time.
